Indianapolis, Indiana  |  651-424-6529  |  [zengtao.wang@lilly.com](mailto:zengtao.wang@lilly.com)  |  [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zengtao-wang)  |  [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=4mJXDH4AAAAJ)  |  [GitHub](https://github.com/zengtaowang)  |  [Personal website](https://zengtaowang.github.io)

## PROFESSIONAL PROFILE

Pharmacometrics and quantitative pharmacology scientist applying population PK/PD, model-based meta-analysis, mechanistic modeling, and simulation to clinical development and trial design across neuroscience and diabetes. At Eli Lilly, works on clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics studies, workflow automation, and emerging AI-augmented workflows. Doctoral research examined the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of amyloid beta peptides and insulin in Alzheimer's disease, with a focus on blood-brain barrier biology and translational pharmacology.

## PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

**Eli Lilly and Company | Sr. Advisor - Pharmacometrician**  
*Indianapolis, IN  |  September 2026-Present  |  Supervisor: Nieves Velez de Mendizabal, PhD*

- Lead pharmacometrics support for clinical development in neuroscience and diabetes, informing study design and regulatory decisions.
- Build automation tools to streamline pharmacometrics workflows and explore AI-augmented approaches.

**Eli Lilly and Company | Advisor - Pharmacometrician**  
*Indianapolis, IN  |  June 2024-August 2026  |  Supervisor: Nieves Velez de Mendizabal, PhD*

- Supported clinical pharmacology studies with quantitative modeling, simulation, and regulatory analyses.

**Biogen Inc. | Modeling and Simulation Co-op**  
*Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacometrics, Cambridge, MA  |  January-June 2023  |  Supervisor: Jingxian (JC) Chen, PhD*

- Built a model-based meta-analysis of MDS-UPDRS outcomes in early Parkinson's disease using aggregated clinical data; developed disease-progression and time-to-event models in NONMEM and Monolix, then simulated endpoint trajectories to inform trial design.
- Developed a population PK/PD model for a Parkinson's disease antisense oligonucleotide and simulated alternative dosing regimens to support dose optimization.
- Presented model assumptions, findings, and applications to internal stakeholders; presented the MBMA work at ACoP14.

## RESEARCH EXPERIENCE

**Blood-brain barrier and Alzheimer's disease research | Graduate Research Assistant**  
*Department of Pharmaceutics, University of Minnesota Twin Cities  |  November 2019-May 2024  |  Advisor: Karunya K. Kandimalla, PhD*

- Developed population PK and mechanistic models to investigate trafficking and accumulation of amyloid-beta isoforms at the blood-brain barrier endothelium; published in Molecular Pharmaceutics.
- Combined flow cytometry, western blotting, and cellular imaging to study amyloid-beta uptake and intracellular trafficking; published in Molecular Pharmacology.
- Established a compartmental PK model to estimate plasma pharmacokinetics of macromolecular tracers from dynamic SPECT/CT heart imaging.
- Analyzed dynamic SPECT/CT and intracellular trafficking data to evaluate the effects of an HDL mimetic peptide and a gut microbiome metabolite on endothelial amyloid-beta accumulation.
- Interpreted time-series transcriptomic data after insulin exposure and developed a quantitative systems pharmacology model linking insulin signaling, VCAM1 expression, and cerebrovascular inflammation.

**CYP1B1 molecular imaging probes | Undergraduate Research Assistant**  
*School of Pharmacy, Shanghai Jiao Tong University  |  October 2016-June 2019  |  Advisor: Qingqing Meng, PhD*

- Synthesized and characterized near-infrared and NIR-PET bimodal probes targeting CYP1B1.
- Evaluated probe binding and selectivity in CYP1B1-overexpressing cancer cells using flow cytometry and confocal microscopy; assessed tumor visualization and biodistribution in vivo.

**Anti-amyloid antibody delivery across the blood-brain barrier | Summer Research Intern**  
*University of Tokyo / Innovation Center of Nanomedicine, Kawasaki, Japan  |  Summer 2018  |  Supervisor: Kazunori Kataoka, PhD*

- Prepared and characterized PEGylated antibodies using gel permeation chromatography and dynamic light scattering; investigated pharmacokinetics and brain accumulation.

## TECHNICAL SKILLS

**Modeling:** Population PK/PD, nonlinear mixed-effects modeling, model-based meta-analysis, time-to-event modeling, quantitative systems pharmacology, clinical trial simulation  
**Automation and AI:** Pharmacometric workflow automation; interest in AI-augmented workflows  
**Software:** NONMEM, Monolix, MATLAB/SimBiology, R, mrgsolve, Phoenix WinNonlin, SAAM II, Stella Architect  
**Laboratory:** Cell culture, permeability assays, ELISA, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, western blotting, HPLC, chemical synthesis
